$comment: Expected outcomes over the recordings in engine-declarations.v1.json. Recorded bodies are never copied here: every response is a pointer {engine, instance?, path} into that file. A path a case does not list answers 404 text/plain "404 page not found"; `unreachable: true` means every request fails at the network layer. Test names carry the RL2-ENGINE-0N id and iterate over caseId. Engines with status pending in the recordings (vLLM) keep status pending here too: tests assert they are still pending and skip them, and nobody hand-writes their responses.

channels.$comment: Channel wire values (RelayRequestedConfig.transport). The channel is connection-level; capabilities are model-level.

fingerprint.$comment: RL2-ENGINE-01. Read-only GETs, all five requested; the status code alone never decides (LM Studio answers 200 + {"error": ...} on unknown paths). A rule hits only on a 2xx JSON object of the stated shape. Exactly one engine hit -> that engine; two or more engine hits -> manual; no engine hit -> generic when the generic rule hits, otherwise manual. Every outcome but manual uses the default channel chat; generic leaves engineProfile empty.

rules.llamacpp: GET /props: object with an object `modalities` or an object `default_generation_settings`
rules.ollama: GET /api/tags: object whose `models` is an array and every row has a string `name`
rules.lmstudio: GET /api/v0/models: object whose `data` is an array and every row has a string `type`
rules.vllm: GET /version: object with a string `version` and no `error` key
rules.generic: GET /v1/models: object whose `data` is an array (consulted only when no engine rule hits)

declarations.$comment: RL2-ENGINE-02. Per-model capability declarations, parsed by the production connector from responses it already requests. Values are true / false / null (null = unknown, stored as an absent key of AIModel.engineDeclaration). Ollama reads `models[].capabilities` of GET /api/tags (identical to POST /api/show in the recording, so no extra request): vision -> image, tools -> toolCall, thinking -> thinking, a missing word is false; a row without the `capabilities` key is all null. LM Studio reads GET /api/v0/models: type vlm -> image true, llm -> image false, embeddings -> not in the chat catalog; `capabilities` containing tool_use -> toolCall true, present without it -> false, key absent -> null; thinking null. llama.cpp reads GET /props once and applies it to every model of the connection: modalities.vision true/false -> image; chat_template_caps.supports_tools true -> toolCall true, false -> null (not a negative declaration); thinking null. vLLM, Open WebUI and generic connections declare nothing: all null. Consumer side: image true -> facade vision_input supported and the composer photo entry visible; image false -> unsupported and hidden; null is left to the Relay unknown rule (U7, not asserted here).

cases.rule: no response body is read: engineProfile vllm yields an empty declaration for any model

thinking.$comment: RL2-ENGINE-04. For a connection with an engineProfile the thinking row is decided by the write-path table, not by the protocol. writable -> the existing chat-template toggle (chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking). Not writable -> the existing notice "Uses the model’s default" (no new copy), except Ollama whose engineDeclaration.thinking is false -> the existing unsupported disclosure. llama.cpp native keeps today's non-Chat notice. Connections without an engineProfile keep the Relay rule unchanged.

edit.$comment: RL2-ENGINE-03. Editing a local connection (one with an engineProfile) keeps engineProfile, securityMode and certificateFingerprint exactly as they were, whatever the edit, including a relay-kind change. A channel change re-verifies the default model; when that verification fails the user value is not discarded: the existing save-as-unverified action stores the new channel and the connection shows the existing unverified state. Channel candidates come from channels.byEngine only.

change.relayKind: any other kind the end offers
